transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Michael Torres (Aurora CISO), Leah Patel (Head of Infrastructure), Samir Rao (DevOps), Naomi Li (Legal)

Summary section (auto-generated):
Jordan: quick intro, we'll focus on security and compliance items you flagged on the form.

00:00 Michael: okay thanks everyone, we're mostly looking at risk and compliance for our telemetry ingestion and downstream analytics, so um primary questions are encryption, audit, and access control, any training use of data, and residency, right
00:18 Jordan: yep, that's what we got in the form, thanks Michael. i'll hand to Priya for the technical layout, then we can dig into docs.
00:27 Priya: hi all, quick runbook — Redwood has hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private/vpc/on-prem. For security posture we provide SOC 2 Type II artifacts, SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC with role templates, full audit logs, and encryption at rest with KMS integrations, plus options for customer-managed keys on Private.
00:45 Leah: when you say customer-managed keys on private, do you mean HSM integration or just KMS? what's the ownership?
00:52 Priya: good question. For Hosted we integrate with our cloud provider KMS; keys are managed by Redwood unless the customer is on Dedicated or Private and purchases the key-management add-on. For Private we support BYOK via customer KMS/HSM — i.e., you keep keys in your KMS and we call them for decryption. sometimes the language in our docs says H-S-M but it's really via KMS provider APIs, we can detail HSM-backed KMS providers.
01:15 Samir: and are the model weights or any artifacts persisted in a way that your team could access them? we need to ensure separation for some regulated data flows
01:22 Priya: by default Redwood does not train on customer data; we explicitly separate training pipelines. For Hosted we maintain operational telemetry but do not use customer prompts for model training. For Dedicated and Private, the customer data stays in your tenancy/network and access is limited to your admins — Redwood ops have an audited, role-based support path.
01:40 Michael: audited path, can you give an example of the SRE support workflow? we need it for our audit team
01:45 Jordan: typical workflow is support ticket -> scoped access via time-limited role -> activity logged in audit trails -> post-action review. We can provide sample logs and the change control process in the SOC2 binder.
01:58 Naomi: about audit logs, retention requirements — we might need 7 years for some telemetry. what retention windows do you support and can we export logs to our SIEM?
02:08 Priya: audit logs are configurable. Out of the box we retain 90 days in the console, you can configure longer retention and export to your SIEM via syslog or S3 delivery; for Dedicated/Private export is straightforward inside your network. Seven years is long — we'd recommend archiving to your own object store; we can automate export.
02:28 Michael: what about immutable logs / tamper-evidence? we have auditors who look for chain-of-custody
02:33 Priya: we support write-once S3 lifecycles and can sign logs; for the highest assurance customers we recommend routing logs to their own secure object store with WORM controls. we'll put sample config for that.
02:46 Leah: SSO integration — we use Okta and require SCIM provisioning. How mature is your SCIM/SCIM2 support?
02:53 Priya: we support SAML2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning; group sync, user deactivation, role mapping to RBAC. There are small gaps sometimes — e.g., some profile attributes mapping needs manual mapping on first sync — but it's standard.
03:10 Samir: RBAC granularity: can we set per-route permissions? like restrict embedding endpoints for some teams
03:17 Priya: yes, per-service and per-route role bindings are supported on Dedicated/Private, Hosted supports per-api-key and per-application roles. For very granular policies we recommend Dedicated where you map your internal groups to Redwood roles.
03:30 Michael: encryption in transit and at rest? TLS is obvious, but at rest do you encrypt per-tenant?
03:35 Priya: in Hosted we encrypt at rest using provider KMS and each customer's data is separated, but key material is managed by Redwood unless you enable customer-managed keys; Dedicated gives you more control, Private you manage keys fully if you want. We also support envelope encryption for additional separation.
03:52 Naomi: legal question — data deletion and retention: if Aurora stops using service, what's the deletion guarantee and do you provide certificate?
03:59 Jordan: we have a documented data deletion policy and we can provide deletion certificates. For Hosted we have the standard 90 day backup retention window; for Dedicated/Private we can tighten that to 30 days or immediate deletion policies per contract. We'll capture precise SLAs in the contract.
04:16 Michael: ok, about data residency — our primary requirement is all telemetry and logs must remain in the EU. Is EU region supported for hosted?
04:23 Priya: yes, we have EU-hosted regions. For strict residency we typically recommend Dedicated in an EU region or Private deployment inside your VPC to ensure no egress. We'll note the available regions and can provide runbooks.
04:40 Leah: PCI? we have some PCI scoped streams; do you have any customers using Redwood for PCI workloads?
04:46 Priya: we have customers in regulated verticals; Redwood itself is not PCI certified as a payment processor, but we can support customers' PCI requirements via Dedicated or Private and contract-level controls — Naomi we can follow-up with examples.
04:58 Michael: incident response and breach notification — timeline? 72 hours is typical for us to notify regulators
05:04 Jordan: Redwood's standard incident response is 24/72 depending on severity; we commit to notifying customers per contract timelines and provide the incident report. We'll share our incident response playbook excerpt.
05:18 Samir: network architecture — if we go Dedicated, do we get VPC peering or private links? how are inbound/outbound controlled?
05:26 Priya: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link depending on cloud provider; egress rules are controlled by customer policy and we support IP allowlists and NAT configuration. For Private deployments you sit fully inside your network.
05:40 Leah: curious about logging of API payloads — customers sometimes want redaction. Can Redwood redact sensitive fields before logs store?
05:48 Priya: yes we have configurable redaction and masking for logs and can set filters to avoid storing PII or specific keys. For Hosted we recommend sending parsing rules during onboarding; for Dedicated/Private easier to implement inline.
06:05 Michael: any pen test or vuln scans we can review?
06:08 Jordan: we run quarterly vulnerability scans and annual pen tests; we can provide high-level reports or summaries and redacted findings. SOC2 Type II covers many of the controls auditors care about.
06:20 Naomi: about third-party subprocessors and data flow — who are your sub-processors and what data do they see?
06:27 Priya: typical subprocessors include cloud infra (AWS/GCP), monitoring providers, and analytics; we'll provide the subprocessor list and their roles. For Dedicated/Private, the list shrinks since infra lives in your tenancy.
06:40 Samir: question — model and prompt caching / KV cache — could that cache leak across tenants? we use tenant isolation strictly
06:46 Priya: cache is per-tenant or per-instance; runtime KV cache is isolated. There have been misreports in some initial docs, but we guarantee isolation at the instance boundary and will show config for caching.
07:00 Michael: do you have a formal data processing agreement and standard contract clauses for EU?
07:06 Jordan: yes we have DPA and SCCs; for EU residency and transfers we have clauses and can support additional addenda.
07:15 Leah: for the pilot we want to run a throughput/latency benchmark against our ingest loads. how do you recommend we scope that?
07:22 Priya: scope: sample dataset, expected QPS, latency SLOs, endpoint types (embedding/generation), region, and whether KV/prefix caching will be used. For Dedicated pilot we can reserve capacity and run synthetic tests. We'll provide a benchmarking template.
07:40 Michael: timeline — we're aiming to decide in 4 weeks and pilot in 6-8 weeks, legal review after security check.
07:48 Jordan: sounds reasonable. we'll get the SOC2 and whitepaper to you within 48 hours and schedule the technical deep-dive.
07:55 Naomi: one more — do you have a delegated admin or break-glass procedure for emergency access?
08:01 Priya: yes we support time-limited emergency access with approval flow and audit logging; again, Dedicated/Private gives stronger contractual guarantees.
08:15 Michael: ok let's recap and next steps
08:18 Jordan: recap — Jordan send SOC2 + security whitepaper; Priya schedule technical deep-dive with Samir; Aurora to fill questionnaire; we'll propose Dedicated pilot scope and pricing. action items and owners in the notes.
08:32 Meeting end.
